<!--
  pr-faq — archived PR-FAQ page.
  Lives at: `product/pr-faqs/<kebab-name>.md`.
  Authorship: canonical. SLO: never — an archived PR-FAQ is a record of its launch, not a living page.
  Owner: fixed to `product`, do not substitute.
  Discipline: the press release stays in past tense, dated to the original launch day, even years later.
  Variants: this is the Mini PR-FAQ — a single consolidated FAQ section, ~one-page press release,
    calibrated for solo-operator / founder scope; the Full canonical Amazon variant splits FAQ into
    "External questions" (press / customer) and "Internal questions" (legal / ops / engineering) — fork
    this template to archive a full-canonical artifact.
  Appends: Post-ship learnings — after the launch has had time to play out (post-release).
  Produced by: /working-backwards — mirrors the domain-side working-backwards PR-FAQ structure and adds a
    post-hoc "Post-ship learnings" section comparing launch reality against the PR-FAQ prediction.
  Disposition: keep every header; "None." when empty; in a section the Appends line above names,
    "Pending: <event>." until that event, naming an event that line declares.
  Substitute: {{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{ORIGINATION}} {{PRODUCT_NAME}}
    {{LAUNCH_DATE}} {{CUSTOMER_SEGMENT}} {{HEADLINE}} {{SUB_HEADLINE}} {{CUSTOMER_NAME}}.
-->

## Product

{{PRODUCT_NAME}}

<!-- The product, feature, or initiative the PR-FAQ covers. Use the customer-facing name, not the internal codename. -->

## Launch date

{{LAUNCH_DATE}}

<!-- The date the press release is dated to. May be the actual ship date or the planned date the PR-FAQ predicted; if they differ, the post-ship learnings section names which. The date a thing ships is PARTITIONED, not owned: this page carries the DATED-TO date. The others are a `roadmap` commitment, a `prd`'s rough timing, a `gtm-plan`'s launch phasing, a `campaign`'s own deadlines, a `pr-faq`'s dated-to date, and a `release-notes` shipped fact — six facts, not six copies of one. See [[_authoring:wiki-fact-ownership#fact-ownership]]. -->

## Customer segment

{{CUSTOMER_SEGMENT}}

## Press release

### {{HEADLINE}}

*{{SUB_HEADLINE}}*

<!-- Past tense, dated to {{LAUNCH_DATE}}. One page maximum. External-facing tone — describes how the world sees the product, not how the team built it. No internal jargon ("leverage", "synergies", "platform", "stack", "robust"). Customer language only. -->

> "Customer quote in the customer's own voice."
> — {{CUSTOMER_NAME}}, {{CUSTOMER_SEGMENT}}

<!-- Quote in the customer's own voice. If the team can't write a believable quote, the value proposition isn't sharp enough. -->

## FAQ

<!-- Minimum 5 question-and-answer pairs. Hard questions only. At least one trade-off question ("what did we give up to ship this?") and at least one "why won't this work" question ("what's the most likely reason this fails?"). Softball questions defeat the purpose. -->

## Kill criteria

<!-- Non-empty. What would have made the team decide NOT to build this? What evidence, if surfaced during the PR-FAQ read, would have stopped the project? A PR-FAQ that can't be killed is theater. -->

## Post-ship learnings

<!-- Filled after the launch has had time to play out. Compare the launch reality to the PR-FAQ prediction:

- Did the headline customer outcome materialize?
- Did the customer quote ring true once real customers used the product?
- Which kill-criteria thresholds were approached? Did the team override any, and was that the right call?
- Which FAQ trade-offs proved larger or smaller than predicted?
- What would the team write differently if drafting this PR-FAQ today? -->
